caution: Published statements only. No automated taxon confirmation, local absence, or certified identification. Claim dates refer to sources, not an updated site survey.

items.label: Name authority and type locality
items.statement: The original description is Bufo mcgregori Taylor, 1922; type locality is near Pasonanca, Zamboanga, Mindanao.
items.limitation: Historical specimen names must be retained in provenance, not silently rewritten.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Ansonia mcgregori

items.label: Published range context
items.statement: The curated taxonomy account places the taxon in mountains of central and western Mindanao.
items.limitation: This does not establish its identity in an individual survey locality.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Ansonia mcgregori

items.label: Species-complex uncertainty
items.statement: A multilocus phylogeographic study detected deeply divergent Mindanao Ansonia lineages, including cryptic lineages in western Mindanao.
items.limitation: Geographic or external similarity does not establish a vetted species identity; genetic/bioacoustic resolution is pending.
items.source: Sanguila et al. 2011, Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution

items.label: Vocal character research
items.statement: Published work has examined variation in advertisement calls within the Mindanao Ansonia species complex.
items.limitation: No validated call-recognition threshold or species-specific audio key is supplied here.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Ansonia mcgregori literature summary

items.label: 2021 taxonomic correction
items.statement: A molecular, morphometric and type-specimen study clarified the name L. magnus for a widespread lower-elevation species and distinguished L. diuatus.
items.limitation: Older reports using L. magnus can refer to a different member of the complex; preserve their original name and date.

items.label: Philippine island records
items.statement: AMNH summarizes records from Basilan, Biliran, Bohol, Camiguin Sur, Dinagat, Leyte, Mindanao and Samar.
items.limitation: The listed elevation range reflects historical records and taxonomic interpretation that requires careful review after the 2021 revision.
items.source: AMNH Amphibian Species of the World, Limnonectes magnus

items.label: Documented Miral River surveys
items.statement: A 2025 anuran survey along Miral River in Bansalan, Davao del Sur, reports the species in a six-species field assemblage.
items.limitation: A study-site record is not evidence of occurrence or encounter probability at another river or station.
items.source: Ubat 2025, Davao del Sur State College institutional thesis

items.label: Fanged-frog species complex
items.statement: The revised complex requires examination of published comparative traits and locality context, rather than identifying all large fanged frogs as L. magnus.
items.limitation: This note contains no newly validated morphological identification key.

items.label: Golden head fur
items.statement: Bat Conservation International describes distinctive gold-colored fur on the head of the giant golden-crowned flying fox.
items.limitation: This character is not sufficient by itself to confirm a distant or silhouetted bat.
items.source: Bat Conservation International, Acerodon jubatus species account

items.label: Fig-rich forest foraging
items.statement: A fecal-analysis study near Subic Bay reported Ficus seeds as predominant components of the diet, supporting forest fruiting-tree dependence.
items.limitation: These food frequencies are from one studied colony and period, not a universal dietary percentage.
items.source: Stier and Mildenstein 2005, Journal of Mammalogy 86:719–728

items.label: Mixed-colony roosting
items.statement: Published species notes report tree roosting, sometimes in colonies with large flying foxes.
items.limitation: Mixed-colony observations demand separate species assessment before assigning counts.
items.source: Bat Conservation International, Acerodon jubatus species account

items.label: Published misidentification case
items.statement: A 2025 Luban Island study reassessed a colony initially identified as A. jubatus and described Pteropus alternatives.
items.limitation: This is a warning about uncertain site IDs, not evidence that A. jubatus is absent from the whole region.
items.source: Ramos and Calica 2025, Davao Research Journal 16(2)

items.label: Separate dated Philippine legal listing
items.statement: A DENR ERDB 2022 reference describes A. jubatus as Critically Endangered under Philippine DAO 2019-09 and Endangered on the IUCN global list.
items.limitation: This is a report of two dated distinct systems, not verification of legal amendments after 2022.

items.label: Accepted genus and former combination
items.statement: The ASM Mammal Diversity Database lists Carlito syrichta, with earlier uses under Tarsius syrichta and original Simia Syrichta.
items.limitation: Historic occurrence records keep their original published identification strings.
items.source: ASM Mammal Diversity Database, Carlito syrichta

items.label: Bohol secondary forest use
items.statement: A radio-telemetry study at Corella, Bohol, documented habitat use within regenerating secondary lowland rainforest.
items.limitation: The observed habitat use is site-specific, not an island-wide habitat preference score.
items.source: Neri-Arboleda, Stott and Arboleda 2002, Journal of Zoology 257:387–402

items.label: Sex-associated home ranges in 1999 field sample
items.statement: The Bohol radio-tracking sample estimated mean home ranges of 6.45 hectares for males and 2.45 hectares for females.
items.limitation: Sample comprised four males and six females, and does not establish a species-wide home-range standard.
items.source: Neri-Arboleda, Stott and Arboleda 2002, Journal of Zoology 257:387–402

items.label: Mindanao forest-fragment features
items.statement: A field study reported that tarsiers in regenerating forest over limestone often used smaller trees and lianas for sleeping and foraging.
items.limitation: Habitat structure is a research observation, not a presence threshold or confirmed observation at a new site.
items.source: Philippine tarsier forest-fragment habitat study, PubMed record 32043166

items.label: Captive-activity study limit
items.statement: A 2019 study characterized captive tarsier activity budgets under male/female and solitary/paired conditions.
items.limitation: Captive behavior must not be presented as a wild-animal detection schedule.
